title: Speccify Playbook v1
description: A playbook captures a complex, recurring workflow: ordered steps, the sources they were researched from, reusable assets and the pitfalls you would otherwise hit twice. It is written for coding agents — the knowledge an agent would have to re-derive every time. Playbooks are directories (bundles): playbook.yaml plus an optional assets/ tree.

schema_version.description: Playbook schema version. Version 1 is a clean restart — the component-spec schema it replaced has no migration path.

id.description: Declared name, '@scope/name'. Where a playbook was fetched from is a lockfile property, not part of its name.

version.description: SemVer. Bump major when steps change in a way that breaks an in-flight run.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what this playbook gets you, and where it starts and ends.

applies_to.description: Selection criteria — how an agent (or `speccify search`) decides this is the right playbook.

prerequisites.description: What must already be true before step one. Checked by a human or agent, not by Speccify.

steps.description: Ordered steps. Order matters: it is the part that is expensive to rediscover.

sources.description: Where the knowledge came from. Every source carries a retrieval date so ageing is measurable.

pitfalls.description: The things you get wrong once. Often the most valuable part of a playbook.

acceptance.description: How to tell the whole playbook succeeded.

id.description: Stable handle — agents and the viewer refer to steps by id.

detail.description: Markdown: what to do, in which order, what to watch out for.

uses.description: Delegate this step to another playbook (reuse). Local id or git source, with optional version range.

sources.description: Ids of entries in the top-level `sources` list.

verify.description: How to tell this step actually worked, before moving on.

retrieved.description: ISO date the source was last checked. `speccify check` warns when it gets stale.

note.description: Which part of the source matters, e.g. a section name.

assetPath.description: Path inside the playbook bundle; always below assets/.
